source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.leaves: Odd-pinnately compound; coriaceous, with 5–11 leaflets (Sophora key)
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Deep violet-blue petals; racemes; corolla 15–16 mm long
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Torulose/knobby, 1–4 fertile segments; brown at maturity; 10–20 mm thick (key)
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Evergreen leathery leaves with 5–11 leaflets vs. thin deciduous leaves of Sophora affinis

cautions: Source uses Sophora secundiflora; repository's existing taxonomic crosswalk lists this as a synonym of Dermatophyllum secundiflorum
Poisonous seeds and flowers reported in Flora; source warnings are not toxicology validation
Historical name and morphology require independent corroboration before identification scoring
Regional distribution statements do not prove Hays County nativity
